findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: The test begins with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` and later calls `time.sleep(0.1)` with the comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change'. Because the monkeypatch replaces `time.sleep` globally, this call returns immediately and provides no settling time. The test then relies on `step.join()` racing the flusher thread to observe the produced message, making the test timing-dependent and flaky — exactly the flakiness the added sleep was presumably meant to fix. Use a real sleep (e.g., import sleep from time before patching, or patch `sentry.spans.consumers.process.flusher.time.sleep` only) or poll until the message appears.

findings.title: join() breaks out of the process loop on deadline expiry, leaving remaining flusher processes unterminated
findings.body: In `join()`, if the deadline expires while waiting for an earlier process, the `break` exits the loop entirely, so all subsequent processes in `self.processes` never get `process.terminate()` called on them. With the new multi-process flusher this can leave several spawned flusher processes running past the join timeout (they are daemon processes, so they die only with the parent, but they continue flushing and producing to Kafka until then). Each process should be terminated even when the deadline has passed, rather than skipping termination for the rest.

findings.title: max_processes=0 is silently treated as 'one process per shard'
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` uses truthiness, so passing `--flusher-processes 0` (or any falsy value) does not mean zero/invalid but instead falls back to spawning one process per shard — the most expensive configuration. The CLI option added in consumers/__init__.py places no lower bound on the value, so a misconfigured deployment would silently scale the flusher to the maximum number of processes. Either validate the option (reject values < 1) or use an explicit `is None` check.
